title: Symbolic powers commute with flat extension to a prime ideal
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal such that its extended ideal $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pS$ is a prime ideal of $S$. For a prime ideal $P$ of a commutative ring $T$ and $n\geq0$, define its symbolic power by $P^{(n)}=\{x\in T:x/1\in P^nT_P\}$, where $T_P$ is localization at the complement of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $P^0=T$. Then for every $n\geq0$ one has $\mathfrak p^{(n)}S=\mathfrak q^{(n)}$.

source.place: Tag 0BC0, lemma-symbolic-power-flat-extension, statement and proof, lines 15578-15615; with the explicit definition from definition-symbolic-power. The Noetherian hypotheses are harmless restrictions of the source statement.

proof.text: For $n=0$ both symbolic powers are the whole ring, so the assertion is immediate. Henceforth fix $n\geq1$. First verify $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$, writing $\varphi:R\to S$ for the given map. For $t\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, multiplication by $t$ is injective on the domain $R/\mathfrak p$. Flat tensor exactness and the quotient-tensor isomorphism identify its tensor with multiplication by $\varphi(t)$ on $S/\mathfrak pS=S/\mathfrak q$, which is therefore injective. Since $\mathfrak q$ is proper, $1\ne0$ in $S/\mathfrak q$, so $\varphi(t)\notin\mathfrak q$. The reverse inclusion $\mathfrak p\subseteq\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ follows from the definition of extension.

proof.text: Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, $k=A/\mathfrak m=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $B=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}S$, and $C=S_{\mathfrak q}$. Step 1 places the denominators of $B$ outside $\mathfrak q$, giving $B\to C$. The localization-tensor statement, applied to $R\to A$ and the $R$-module $S$, gives $A\otimes_RS\cong B$, $(r/t)\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(r)s/\varphi(t)$ (identify $R\otimes_RS$ with $S$ by $r\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(r)s$). Consequently cancellation of base change gives, for each $A$-module $H$, a canonical $S$-linear isomorphism $H\otimes_RS\cong H\otimes_AB$, $h\otimes s\mapsto h\otimes(s/1)$. These formulas show that all maps respect multiplication by elements of $S$. The cited prime-localization statement supplies the local ring $A$ and its residue field $k$.

source.place: Tag 0BC0, lemma-symbolic-power-flat-extension, first paragraph, notation S_p and the tensor description of localization; Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule)

proof.text: By the definition of symbolic power, $\ker(R\to A/\mathfrak m^n)=\mathfrak p^{(n)}$. Tensor the exact sequence $0\to\mathfrak p^{(n)}\to R\to A/\mathfrak m^n$ with the flat $R$-module $S$. Its first image in $S$ is exactly $\mathfrak p^{(n)}S$: the map sends $x\otimes s$ to $\varphi(x)s$, and its image consists of finite sums of such terms. By step 2 and the quotient-tensor isomorphism, $(A/\mathfrak m^n)\otimes_RS\cong(A/\mathfrak m^n)\otimes_AB\cong B/\mathfrak m^nB$. Under these maps the tensor of $R\to A/\mathfrak m^n$ is $s\mapsto s/1\bmod\mathfrak m^nB$. Thus $\mathfrak p^{(n)}S=\ker(S\to B/\mathfrak m^nB)$.

source.place: Tag 0BC0, lemma-symbolic-power-flat-extension, first two sentences: tensoring the kernel

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq n$ let $F_i=\mathfrak m^i/\mathfrak m^n\subseteq A/\mathfrak m^n$ and let $E_i$ be the image of $F_i\otimes_RS$ in $(A/\mathfrak m^n)\otimes_RS=B/\mathfrak m^nB$. Flat tensor exactness makes these inclusions injective and gives $E_0=B/\mathfrak m^nB$, $E_n=0$, and $E_i/E_{i+1}\cong G_i\otimes_RS$ for $0\leq i<n$, where $G_i=\mathfrak m^i/\mathfrak m^{i+1}$. Indeed tensor the short exact sequences $0\to F_{i+1}\to F_i\to G_i\to0$. Surjectivity of the last tensor map can also be checked by lifting the first factors of each finite sum of pure tensors. Step 2 identifies $G_i\otimes_RS$ with $G_i\otimes_AB$. All these identifications are $S$-linear, hence commute with multiplication by $f\in S$.

source.place: Tag 0BC0, lemma-symbolic-power-flat-extension, finite filtration paragraph and its first displayed isomorphism

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m$ annihilates $G_i$, so the quotient-ring tensor statement gives $G_i\otimes_AB\cong G_i\otimes_kD$, where $D=B/\mathfrak mB$. The fraction map identifies $D\cong(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(S/\mathfrak q)$: it sends $s/\varphi(t)$ to $\bar s/\bar\varphi(t)$, and its inverse is induced by the same fraction formula. Step 1 says all these denominators are nonzero in the domain $S/\mathfrak q$; thus $D$ is a nonzero domain. Explicitly a fraction is zero only if a nonzero denominator multiple of its numerator is zero, and the domain law forces that numerator to be zero. In particular each $f\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ has nonzero image in $D$. Choose a $k$-basis $(e_j)$ of $G_i$ by the vector-space freeness statement. Every element of $G_i\otimes_kD$ has a unique finite expression $\sum_j e_j\otimes d_j$: existence follows by expanding first factors in the basis, and uniqueness by applying the coordinate linear forms tensored with $D$. If $f\sum_j e_j\otimes d_j=0$, each $\bar f d_j=0$ in the domain $D$, so all $d_j=0$. Therefore multiplication by $f$ is injective on every $E_i/E_{i+1}$.

For $f\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, descending induction on $i$ proves that $f$ acts injectively on $E_i$. The base $E_n=0$ is immediate. If $fx=0$ in $E_i$, its class in $E_i/E_{i+1}$ is zero by step 5, so $x\in E_{i+1}$ and the induction hypothesis gives $x=0$. Hence every such $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $E_0=B/\mathfrak m^nB$. proof.text: Extension commutes with products of ideals by expanding finite sums of products of generators. Consequently $\mathfrak q^nC=(\mathfrak pS)^nC=\mathfrak p^nC=\mathfrak m^nC$. The defining kernel of $\mathfrak q^{(n)}$ is therefore $\ker(S\to C/\mathfrak m^nC)$. Since the map in step 6 is injective, this kernel equals $\ker(S\to B/\mathfrak m^nB)$, which step 3 identified as $\mathfrak p^{(n)}S$. This proves the assertion for every $n\geq1$, and step 1 handled $n=0$.
